Talent Strategy: Enabling Growth Through People
paragraphs: In this Annual Report on Form 10-K, Covista Inc. (formerly known as Adtalem Global Education Inc.), together with its subsidiaries, is collectively referred to as "Covista," "we," "our," "us," or similar references. Covista was incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware in August 1987. Our executive offices are located at 233 South Wacker Drive, Chicago, Illinois, 60606, and the telephone number is (312) 651-1400.

Covista is America's largest healthcare educator, serving 100,000 students and supported by an alumni network of 400,000 across five accredited institutions: Chamberlain University ("Chamberlain"), Walden University ("Walden"), American University of the Caribbean School of Medicine ("AUC"), Ross University School of Medicine ("RUSM"), and Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine ("RUSVM"). Covista delivers education to its students at multiple campuses and online.
Covista's purpose is to open doors and unlock potential for its students through educational programs across nursing, medicine, veterinary medicine, the social and behavioral sciences, and more.

Covista's strategy, which it refers to as "Purpose at Scale," is centered on expanding access to healthcare education and helping address the U.S. healthcare workforce shortage. This strategy is built around four core principles: operational excellence, platform extension, employer integration, and technology focus.
We present three reportable segments as follows:

Walden – This segment includes the operations of Walden, which offers degree and certificate programs, including those in nursing, education, counseling, business, information technology, psychology, public health, social work and human services, public administration and public policy, and criminal justice.

Medical and Veterinary – This segment includes the operations of AUC, RUSM, and RUSVM, collectively referred to as the "medical and veterinary schools," which offer degree and certificate programs in the medical and veterinary postsecondary education industry.

Chamberlain was founded in 1889 as Deaconess College of Nursing and acquired by Covista in 2005. In May 2017, Chamberlain College of Nursing broadened its reach in healthcare education through the establishment of Chamberlain University and now offers its programs through its College of Nursing and College of Health Professions.

Chamberlain's nursing degree offerings include a three-year onsite and online pre-licensure Bachelor of Science in Nursing ("BSN") degree, an online post-licensure BSN degree completion option for Registered Nurses ("RN-BSN"), an online Master of Science in Nursing ("MSN") degree, including Nurse Practitioner tracks and other specialties, and the online Doctor of Nursing Practice ("DNP") degree.

Through its College of Health Professions, Chamberlain offers an online Master of Public Health ("MPH") degree program, an online Master of Social Work ("MSW") degree program, and an onsite Master of Physician Assistant Studies ("MPAS") degree program.

Chamberlain provides an educational experience distinguished by a high level of care for students, academic excellence, and integrity delivered through its 24 campuses and online. Chamberlain is committed to graduating health professionals who are empowered to transform healthcare delivery.

Chamberlain's pre-licensure BSN program enables students to complete their degree in three years of full-time study as opposed to the typical four-year BSN program with summer breaks. Beginning in September 2019, Chamberlain began offering an evening/weekend BSN option at select campuses. In September 2020, Chamberlain launched its online BSN option that offers a blend of flexibility, interactivity, and experiential learning.

Students who already have passed their National Council Licensure Examination ("NCLEX") exam and achieved RN designation through a diploma or associate degree can complete their BSN degree online through Chamberlain's RN-BSN completion option in three semesters of full-time study, although most students enroll part-time while they continue working as nurses.

The online MSN degree program offers five non-direct-care specialty tracks: Nurse Educator, Nurse Executive, Nursing Informatics, Population Health, and Healthcare Policy. The accelerated MSN program offers concentrations in Clinical Nurse Leadership, Advanced Nursing Leadership, and Advanced Nursing Leadership with Artificial Intelligence. The accelerated RN-MSN program provides associate or diploma-prepared RNs the opportunity to earn an MSN, rather than a BSN, with the same concentration options available.

headings: Risks Related to Covista's Regulated Industry
Government budgetary pressures and changes to laws governing financial aid programs could reduce our student enrollment or delay our receipt of tuition payments.
Our ability to comply with some ED regulations is affected by economic forces affecting our students and graduates that are not entirely within our control.
If we fail to maintain our institutional accreditation or if our institutional accrediting body loses recognition by ED, we would lose our ability to participate in Title IV programs.
A bankruptcy filing by us or by any of our Title IV institutions, or a closure of one of our Title IV institutions, would lead to an immediate loss of eligibility to participate in Title IV programs.
Excessive student loan defaults could result in the loss of eligibility to participate in Title IV programs.
Our Title IV institutions could lose their eligibility to participate in federal student financial aid programs if the percentage of their revenue derived from those programs was too high.
If we fail to maintain any of our state authorizations, we would lose our ability to operate in that state and could lose eligibility to participate in Title IV programs in that state.
We could be subject to sanctions if we fail to calculate accurately and make timely payment of refunds of Title IV program funds for students who withdraw before completing their educational program.
Release of confidential information could subject us to civil penalties or cause us to lose our eligibility to participate in Title IV programs.
We could be subject to sanctions if we fail to accurately and timely report sponsored students' tuition, fees, and enrollment to the sponsoring agency.
We are subject to risks relating to enrollment of students. If we are not able to continue to successfully recruit and retain our students, our revenue may decline.
If our graduates are unable to find appropriate employment opportunities or obtain professional licensure or certification, we may not be able to recruit new students.
We face heightened competition in the postsecondary education market from both public and private educational institutions.

Outbreaks of communicable infections or diseases, or other public health pandemics in the locations in which we, our students, faculty, and employees live, work, and attend classes, could substantially harm our business.
Natural disasters or other extraordinary events, political disruptions, armed conflicts or wars may interrupt our operations, cause us to close some of our schools, or suffer casualty losses.
The personal information that we collect may be vulnerable to breach, theft, or loss that could adversely affect our reputation and operations.
System disruptions and vulnerability from security risks to our computer network or information systems could severely impact our ability to serve our existing students and attract new students.
A breach of our information technology systems could subject us to liability, reputational damage, or interrupt the operation of our business.
Government regulations relating to the internet could increase our cost of doing business and affect our ability to grow.
Our ability to open new campuses, offer new programs, and add capacity is dependent on regulatory approvals and requires financial and human resources.
We may not be able to attract, retain, and develop key employees necessary for our operations and the successful execution of our strategic plans.
We may not be able to successfully integrate acquisitions.
paragraphs: Covista's business operations are subject to numerous risks and uncertainties, some of which are not entirely within our control. Investors should carefully consider the risk factors described below and all other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K before making an investment decision with respect to Covista's common stock. If any of the following risks are realized, Covista's business, results of operations, financial condition, and cash flows could be materially and adversely affected, and as a result, the price of Covista's common stock could be materially and adversely
affected. Management cannot predict all the possible risks and uncertainties that may arise. Risks and uncertainties that may affect Covista's business include the following:

We are subject to regulatory audits, investigations, lawsuits, or other proceedings relating to compliance by the institutions in the Covista portfolio with numerous laws and regulations in U.S. and foreign jurisdictions applicable to the postsecondary education industry.

Due to the regulated nature of proprietary postsecondary institutions, we are subject to audits, compliance reviews, inquiries, complaints, investigations, claims of non-compliance, and lawsuits by federal and state governmental agencies, regulatory agencies, accrediting agencies, present and former students and employees, shareholders, and other third parties, any of whom may allege violations of any of the legal and regulatory requirements applicable to us. If the results of any such claims, actions, or allegations thereof are unfavorable to us or one or more of our institutions, we may be required to pay monetary judgments, fines, or penalties, be required to repay funds received under Title IV programs or state financial aid programs, have restrictions placed on or terminate our schools' or programs' eligibility to participate in Title IV programs or state financial aid programs, have limitations placed on or terminate our schools' operations or ability to grant degrees and certificates, have our schools' accreditations restricted or revoked, or be subject to civil or criminal penalties. ED regulations regarding financial responsibility provide that, if any one of our Title IV institutions is unable to pay its obligations under its Program Participation Agreement ("PPA") as a result of operational issues and/or an enforcement action, our other Title IV institutions, regardless of their compliance with applicable laws and regulations, would not be able to maintain their Title IV eligibility without assisting in the repayment of the non-compliant institution's Title IV obligations. As a result, even though Covista's Title IV institutions are operated through independent entities, an enforcement action against one of our institutions could also have a material adverse effect on the businesses, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows of Covista's other Title IV institutions.

The ongoing regulatory effort aimed at all Title IV participating institutions could be a catalyst for additional or more restrictive legislative or regulatory restrictions, investigations, enforcement actions, and claims.

At times, Title IV participating institutions, from all sectors, have experienced scrutiny from federal and state legislators, agencies, attorneys general, and other government officials. An adverse disposition of these existing inquiries, administrative actions, or claims, or the initiation of other inquiries, administrative actions, or claims, could, directly or indirectly, have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows and result in significant restrictions on us and our ability to operate.

paragraphs: This management's discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations ("MD&A") should be read with and is qualified in its entirety by the Consolidated Financial Statements and the notes thereto included in this report. It should also be read in conjunction with the Cautionary Disclosure Regarding Forward-Looking Statements (see the Introduction section preceding Part I), the Risk Factors (see Item 1A. "Risk Factors"), and the Financial Aid and Legislative and Regulatory Requirements (see Item 1. "Business") disclosures set forth in this report. Covista reports on a fiscal year period ending on June 30.

Throughout this MD&A, we sometimes use information derived from the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8. "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" and the notes thereto but not presented in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles ("GAAP"). Certain of these items are considered "non-GAAP financial measures" under the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC") rules. See the "Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Reconciliations"
section for the reasons we use these non-GAAP financial measures and the reconciliations to their most directly comparable GAAP financial measures.

Certain items presented in tables may not sum due to rounding. Percentages presented are calculated from the underlying numbers in thousands. Discussions throughout this MD&A are based on continuing operations unless otherwise noted.

The following discussion is on the comparison between fiscal year 2026 and fiscal year 2025 results. For a discussion on the comparison between fiscal year 2025 and fiscal year 2024 results, see the MD&A included in Covista's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, as filed with the SEC.
We present three reportable segments as follows:

Walden – This segment includes the operations of Walden, which offers degree and certificate programs, including those in nursing, education, counseling, business, information technology, psychology, public health, social work and human services, public administration and public policy, and criminal justice.

Medical and Veterinary – This segment includes the operations of AUC, RUSM, and RUSVM, collectively referred to as the "medical and veterinary schools," which offer degree and certificate programs in the medical and veterinary postsecondary education industry.

"Home Office" includes activities not allocated to a reportable segment. Financial and descriptive information about Covista's reportable segments is presented in Note 19 "Segment Information" to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8. "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data."
Financial and operational highlights for fiscal year 2026 include:
● Covista revenue increased 9.3%, or $165.8 million, to $1,954.1 million in fiscal year 2026 compared to the prior year driven by increased revenue across all segments.

● Net income increased 6.1%, or $14.5 million, to $251.6 million in fiscal year 2026 compared to the prior year. This increase was primarily driven by an increase in revenue along with decreases in interest expense and asset impairments, partially offset by a loss from discontinued operations and increases in strategic advisory costs, labor and other costs to support increased enrollment, marketing expense, investments to support growth initiatives, and the provision for income taxes.
● Diluted earnings per share increased 13.9%, or $0.86, to $7.04 in fiscal year 2026 compared to the prior year driven by the increase in net income and lower diluted shares due to share repurchases.

● Adjusted net income increased 15.3%, or $39.1 million, to $294.7 million in fiscal year 2026 compared to the prior year. This increase was primarily driven by an increase in revenue and a decrease in interest expense, partially offset by increases in labor and other costs to support increased enrollment, marketing expense, investments to support growth initiatives, and the provision for income taxes.

headings: Chamberlain – 此應報告分部包含 Chamberlain 的營運，其提供護理及健康專業領域之進修教育學位及證書課程。
Talent Strategy: Enabling Growth Through People
paragraphs: 本年度10-K申報書中，Covista Inc.（原名為Adtalem Global Education Inc.）及其子公司合稱為"Covista"、"我們"、"我們的"、"我們公司"或類似稱謂。Covista於1987年8月根據特拉華州法律成立。我們的總部位於伊利諾州芝加哥市南華盛頓大道233號，郵遞區號60606，電話號碼為(312) 651-1400。

Covista是美國規模最大的醫療教育機構，服務10萬名學生，並透過40萬名校友網路支持，其教育機構為五所經認證的學院：Chamberlain University（"Chamberlain"）、Walden University（"Walden"）、American University of the Caribbean School of Medicine（"AUC"）、Ross University School of Medicine（"RUSM"）以及Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine（"RUSVM"）。Covista透過多個校區與線上方式為學生提供教育。
Covista的宗旨是透過跨護理、醫學、獸醫醫學、社會與行為科學等領域的教育方案，為學生打開大門並啟發潛能。
Covista的策略，其稱為"Purpose at Scale"，以擴大醫療教育的可近性並協助解決美國醫療人力短缺問題為核心。此策略建立在四大核心原則之上：運營卓越、平台延伸、僱主整合與科技聚焦。
我們提供三個應報告分部如下：
Walden – 此分部包含Walden的運營，提供學位與證書課程，包括護理、教育、諮商、商業、資訊科技、心理學、公共衛生、社會工作與人際服務、公共行政與公共政策以及刑事司法等領域的課程。
醫療與獸醫 – 此分部包含AUC、RUSM與RUSVM的運營，合稱為"醫療與獸醫學院"，提供醫療與獸醫後續教育產業的學位與證書課程。

Chamberlain於1889年成立為Deaconess College of Nursing，並於2005年被Covista收購。2017年5月，Chamberlain College of Nursing透過成立Chamberlain University擴大其在醫療教育的影響力，目前其課程透過College of Nursing與College of Health Professions提供。
Chamberlain 的護理學學位課程包含三年的現場與線上預許可學士護理學位（"BSN"），線上預許可 BSN 學位完成選項（"RN-BSN"）供已取得註冊護理師（"RN"）資格的護理師，線上碩士護理學位（"MSN"），包括護理師專門護理師（"NP"）課程及其他專門領域，以及線上博士護理實踐學位（"DNP"）學位。
透過其健康專業學院，Chamberlain 提供線上公共衛生碩士（"MPH"）學位課程、線上社會工作碩士（"MSW"）學位課程，以及現場醫療助理研究碩士（"MPAS"）學位課程。
Chamberlain 提供以高標準照顧學生、學術卓越與誠信為特色的教育體驗，透過其 24 個校區與線上進行。Chamberlain 承諾培養具備能力的健康專業人才，以轉變醫療照護的提供方式。
Chamberlain 的預許可 BSN 課程讓學生能在三年的全時間學習中完成學位，與通常需要四年並包含暑假的 BSN 課程不同。自 2019 年 9 月起，Chamberlain 開始在部分校區提供晚上及週末的 BSN 選項。2020 年 9 月，Chamberlain 發起線上 BSN 選項，提供靈活性、互動性與實務學習的結合。
已通過國家護理許可考試（"NCLEX"）並透過文憑或副學士學位取得 RN 資格的學生，可透過 Chamberlain 的 RN-BSN 完成選項，在三個全時間學期內完成 BSN 學位，雖然大多數學生在繼續擔任護理師的同時以半時間方式入學。

線上 MSN 學位課程提供五種非直接照護專門領域：護理教育者、護理行政、護理資訊學、人口健康與醫療政策。加速 MSN 課程提供 Clinical Nurse Leadership、Advanced Nursing Leadership 及 Advanced Nursing Leadership with Artificial Intelligence 的專長方向。加速 RN-MSN 課程讓具副學士或文憑資格的 RN 有機會取得 MSN，而非 BSN，並享有相同的專長方向選項。

paragraphs: 本公司的管理層討論與分析（"MD&A"）財務狀況及營運成果應與本報告所附的合併財務報表及其附註一併閱讀，並以之為準。同時，也應與本報告中所列的風險因素（見第1A項"風險因素"）及財務援助與立法與監管要求（見第1項"業務"）等申報資訊一併閱讀。Covista依財務年度為會計期間，財務年度結算日為6月30日。
在本MD&A中，我們有時會使用來自第8項"財務報表與補充資料"所附合併財務報表及其附註的資訊，但這些資訊並未依照美國通用會計準則（"GAAP"）編製。根據美國證券交易委員會（"SEC"）的規則，其中某些項目被視為"非GAAP財務指標"。請參閱"非GAAP財務指標與重編"
本節說明我們使用這些非GAAP財務指標的原因，以及其與最直接可比的GAAP財務指標的調整數額。
部分表格中呈現的項目可能因四捨五入而無法完全相加。百分比係根據萬位數字計算得出。本文件中MD&A各處的討論均基於持續經營業務，除非另有說明。
以下討論為比較財務年度2026與財務年度2025之結果。有關比較財務年度2025與財務年度2024之結果之討論，請參閱Covista於財務年度2025年6月30日結算之年度報告（Form 10-K）中之MD&A部分，該報告已向SEC提交。
我們提供三個應報告分部，如下所述：
Walden – 此分部包含Walden之營運，提供學位及證書課程，包括護理、教育、諮商、商業、資訊科技、心理學、公共衛生、社會工作及人際服務、公共行政與公共政策，以及刑事正義等領域之課程。
Medical and Veterinary – 此分部包含AUC、RUSM及RUSVM之營運， collectively referred to as the "medical and veterinary schools," 提供醫學及獸醫後續教育產業之學位及證書課程。
"Home Office" 包含未分配至應報告分部的活動。關於 Covista 應報告分部的財務與描述性資訊，請參閱第 8 項 "財務報表與補充資料" 中的附註 19 "分部資訊"。
財務與營運重點為 2026 財年包含：
● Covista 營業收入增加 9.3%，即 165.8 百萬美元，至 1,954.1 百萬美元，於財務年度 2026 年相比前一年，因各應報告分部收入均有成長。
● 淨收入增加 6.1%，即 14.5 百萬美元，至 251.6 百萬美元，於財務年度 2026 年相比前一年。此增加主要因收入增加，以及利息費用與資產減損費用減少，部分抵銷因停業業務造成的損失，以及因學生人數增加而導致的策略諮詢費用、人力與其他費用、行銷費用、成長計畫投資，以及所得稅費用的增加。
● 稀釋每股盈餘增加 13.9%，即 0.86 美元，至 7.04 美元，於財務年度 2026 年相比前一年，因淨收入增加以及因股票回購導致稀釋股數減少。
● 調整後淨收入增加 15.3%，即 39.1 百萬美元，至 294.7 百萬美元，於財務年度 2026 年相比前一年。此增加主要因收入增加以及利息費用減少，部分抵銷因學生人數增加而導致的人力與其他費用、行銷費用、成長計畫投資，以及所得稅費用的增加。

headings: 與 Covista 被規範產業相關的風險
政府預算壓力及影響財務補助計畫法律的變更，可能減少我們的學生入學人數或延遲我們收到學費的時間。
我們遵守某些 ED 規範的能力，受到影響我們學生及畢業生的經濟因素影響，而這些因素並非完全在我們的控制範圍內。
如果我們未能維持機構認證或我們的機構認證機構失去 ED 的認可，我們將失去參與 Title IV 計畫的能力。
我們或我們任何 Title IV 學校的破產聲請，或我們任何 Title IV 學校關閉，將導致立即失去參與 Title IV 計畫的資格。
學生貸款過度違約可能導致失去參與 Title IV 計畫的資格。
我們的 Title IV 學校如果來自這些計畫的收入比例過高，可能會失去參與聯邦學生財務補助計畫的資格。
如果我們未能維持任何州的授權，我們將失去在該州運作的能力，並可能失去在該州參與 Title IV 計畫的資格。
我們若未能準確計算並及時支付退還 Title IV 計畫資金，可能面臨處罰，這些資金是針對在完成教育課程前退學的學生。
若我們洩露機密資訊，可能面臨民事處罰，或導致我們失去參與 Title IV 計畫的資格。
我們若未能準確且及時向贊助機構報告受資助學生的學費、費用及註冊情況，可能面臨處罰。
與 Covista 事業相關的風險
我們面臨學生註冊的風險。若我們無法持續成功招募並留住學生，我們的營業收入可能下降。
若我們的畢業生無法找到適當的就業機會，或無法取得專業執照或認證，我們可能無法招募新學生。
我們在後設教育市場面臨來自公私立教育機構的激烈競爭。
我們、學生、教師及員工所處地區若發生傳染性疾病或疫情等公共衛生危機，可能對我們的業務造成重大損害。
自然災害或其他特殊事件、政治動盪、武裝衝突或戰爭可能幹擾我們的營運，導致我們關閉部分學校，或遭受財產損失。
我們所收集的個人資料可能面臨資料外洩、竊取或遺失的風險，這可能會對我們的聲譽及營運造成不利影響。
系統中斷及電腦網路或資訊系統對安全風險的脆弱性，可能嚴重影響我們服務現有學生及吸引新學生的能力。
我們資訊科技系統的資料外洩，可能使我們面臨法律責任、聲譽損害，或幹擾我們的營運。
與互聯網相關的政府法規可能提高我們的營運成本，並影響我們的成長能力。
我們開設新校區、提供新課程及增加容量的能力，取決於法規審批，並需要財務及人力資源。
我們可能無法吸引、留住並培養對我們營運及戰略計畫成功執行至關重要的關鍵員工。
我們可能無法成功整合收購的企業。
paragraphs: Covista 的營運業務面臨許多風險與不確定性，其中一些並非完全在本公司控制範圍內。投資人應謹慎考量下列風險因素及本年度報告表 10-K 所包含的所有資訊，再做是否投資本公司普通股的決定。若任何下列風險實現，將可能對本公司業務、營運成果、財務狀況與現金流造成重大且不利的影響，進而使本公司普通股的價格產生重大且不利的影響。
本公司無法預測所有可能出現的風險與不確定性。可能影響本公司業務的風險與不確定性包括以下內容：
本公司需面對與 Covista 投資組閤中機構遵守美國與外國司法管轄區適用於後設教育產業法律與法規相關的監管審計、調查、訴訟或其他程序。

由於 proprietary 後設教育機構具有受監管的性質，本公司需面對由聯邦與州政府機構、監管機構、認證機構、現任與前任學生與員工、股東及其他第三方提出的審計、合規審查、詢問、投訴、調查、非合規指控與訴訟，任何一方都可能聲稱本公司違反適用於我們的法律與法規要求。若任何上述聲請、行動或指控的結果對本公司或我們的機構不利，本公司可能需支付賠償金、罰款或處罰，需歸還根據第 IV 章計畫所收到的資金或州財政補助資金，對我們學校或計畫參與第 IV 章計畫或州財政補助計畫的資格設限或終止，對我們學校的運作或授予學位與證書的能力設限或終止，對我們學校的認證設限或撤銷，或面臨民事或刑事處罰。根據教育部（ED）關於財務責任的法規，若我們的任何一所第 IV 章計畫機構因運營問題及/或執法行動而無法支付其在計畫參與協議（"PPA"）下的義務，則我們的其他第 IV 章計畫機構，即使其符合適用法律與法規，也無法維持其第 IV 章計畫資格，除非協助償還該非合規機構的第 IV 章計畫義務。因此，即使本公司第 IV 章計畫機構是透過獨立實體運作，對我們其中一所機構的執法行動也可能對本公司其他第 IV 章計畫機構的業務、財務狀況、營運成果與現金流造成重大且不利的影響。
針對所有第 IV 章計畫參與機構持續進行的監管行動，可能成為引發更多或更嚴格立法與法規限制、調查、執法行動與聲請的催化劑。
有時，來自各產業的第 IV 章計畫參與機構會受到聯邦與州立法者、機構、律師總長及其他政府官員的審查。這些現有調查、行政行動或聲請的不利結果，或啟動其他調查、行政行動或聲請，可能直接或間接對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果與現金流造成重大且不利的影響，並導致本公司及其運作能力受到重大限制。
